turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_max_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_max_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST yield strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**1. Processing dominates.** Grouping training targets by heat treatment and route shows a clear hierarchy:

- **solution_aged** is the best treatment: it holds nearly all the top values (712.9, 697.9, 693.9, 676.7, 674.2, 668.2, 652.3, 648.7, 648.6, 647.2 MPa...). quench_temper is second (~430–610), quenched third, **annealed clearly worst** (many of the lowest values, 96–300 MPa).
- **Route: wrought > AM > cast.** Almost every sample above 640 MPa is solution_aged + wrought; the best solution_aged + AM values are ~620–640 (e.g., 637.6, 619.4).
- **Aging temperature ~600–740 °C is favorable** for solution_aged parts (all top-10 samples have aging_temp 560–710).

**2. Composition sweet spot in the top samples:**
- C ≲ 0.6 (C ≈ 1.2 is consistently bad), Al ≲ 1.2 (Al = 2.0 shows up in most low rows), Cr ≲ 15 (Cr = 22 rows are weak), Ni ~5–18, moderate Mo (~0–4), Co helpful up to ~10, Ti/V not harmful in moderation.

**3. Matching pool candidates to the best training neighbors:**

| Candidate | Treatment/route | Key match | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| **c072** | sol_aged, wrought | Nearly identical to the 697.9 MPa sample (C 0.32, Ni 9.3, Mo 2.7, Co 7.4, Al 0.05, aging 750) | ~660–700 |
| **c008** | sol_aged, wrought | Twin of the 648.6/712.9 MPa samples (C 0.45, Ni 13, Mo 3.9, Co 8.4, Al 0.12, aging 683) | ~650–690 |
| **c038** | sol_aged, wrought | Close to the 652.3 MPa sample (C 0.57, Cr 4.9, Ni 11.4, low Mo/Al, aging 608) | ~620–650 |
| **c033** | sol_aged, AM | AM analog of the 648.7 MPa recipe (C 0, Cr 9.1, Ni 11, Co 7.6, aging 640, fast cooling); best AM training values reach 637 | ~600–640 |
| **c021** | sol_aged, wrought | Similar to the 591.4/652.3 MPa samples (C 0, Cr 13.4, Ni 7.8, Al 0, aging 592) | ~590–630 |

Runners-up: c009 and c075 (solution_aged AM, good compositions, ~580–620); c015 and c053 penalized by Al ≈ 2.0; quench_temper candidates (c028, c050) cap out near ~540 based on their closest training twins; all annealed candidates were excluded.

Final: c072, c008, c038, c033, c021
